title: Script Editor: When docs in tooltip is disabled, only display tooltip if diagnostics exist
body:

## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

- Closes #123687

## Additional information

<!--
Provide additional information and explanation of your PR, including areas that you are uncertain of or require special attention from reviewers. For examples, please read our pull request guidelines: https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/development/contribution_rules.html#explain-your-contributions
-->

Previously, logic for spawning the script editor tooltip included a bit like:
```cpp
if (!enable_docs || p_symbol.is_empty()) {
    if (enable_diagnostics) {
        // show tooltip with diagnostics
    }
    return;
}
```
I think the intent with this logic was to say, "if there's nothing to show documentation-wise, but we have diagnostics enabled, then show diagnostics!"

However, this can lead to the case where a tooltip is spawned when the hovered symbol is empty _and_ there are no actual diagnostics to show despite diagnostics themselves being enabled.

With this PR, the logic is simplified to:
```cpp
if (!enable_docs) {
    if (!diagnostic_strings_concatenated.is_empty()) {
        // show tooltip with diagnostics
    }
    return;
}
```
This is much simpler: if documentation isn't enabled, then we only show the tooltip if there is any diagnostic data _to display_. (There's guaranteed to be no such data if diagnostics are disabled, since all of the additions to `diagnostic_strings_concatenated` are done inside a check on `enable_diagnostics`.)

If documentation _is_ enabled, then code down below (untouched for this PR) only spawns the tooltip if:
- The documentation symbol being hovered is not empty, OR
- There's a debug value to display at this location, OR
- There's diagnostic data to display at this location

which is the behavior from before #120726, not including the addition of the diagnostic data of course.
